_comment: Book RAG evaluation suite. Consumed by scripts/eval-rag.ps1 (runs the suite) and scripts/eval_metrics.py (re-scores a saved results file). Schema and rules: evals/README.md. Expected ids MUST be book_ids that exist in samples/books.csv; -ValidateOnly proves that offline.
description: Core retrieval-quality suite over the 20-book sample catalogue.

questions.question: Dune by Frank Herbert
questions.note: Soundness check: the literal title+author must retrieve its own book. A failure here means the embedding path or the index is broken, not that the model is picky.

questions.question: Neuromancer by William Gibson
questions.note: Soundness check, second data point.

questions.question: Piranesi by Susanna Clarke
questions.note: Soundness check across a different genre.

questions.question: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind by Yuval Noah Harari
questions.note: Soundness check on non-fiction with a subtitle.

questions.question: The Design of Everyday Things by Don Norman
questions.note: Soundness check on non-fiction; the description is short, so it also probes chunk quality.

questions.question: I loved Dune - recommend something similar.
questions.note: Cross-book recommendation. Dune itself is an allowed mention, not a hit.

questions.question: I want dense political worldbuilding like Le Guin.
questions.note: Le Guin is named as a taste anchor; her own book is the expected hit.

questions.question: Something cyberpunk with hackers and corporate decay.
questions.note: Taste phrasing, not the genre word: the corpus has no 'cyberpunk' genre, only a tag.

questions.question: A space opera full of politics and scheming.
questions.note: Second route into the same cluster; checks that the cluster is reachable from more than one wording.

questions.question: Something quiet and strange with a puzzle at the centre of it.
questions.note: Tone-based request with a single best answer.

questions.question: A thriller with an unreliable narrator about a marriage.
questions.note: Single-answer taste request in a genre with one book.

questions.question: Something short and funny, nothing bleak.
questions.note: The page-count constraint is NOT understood by vector search - it ranks by meaning. This measures that known gap instead of hiding it; see evals/README.md 'Known gaps'.

questions.question: Classic detective fiction with atmosphere and fog.
questions.note: Two-book cluster in one genre.

questions.question: What do you have in Mystery?
questions.note: Catalogue-style question. With -Mode retrieve this is a genre filter; with -Mode agent the agent may answer through List Library instead of vector search.

questions.question: Anything by Kazuo Ishiguro.
questions.note: Author lookup - vector search handles this poorly by design, which is why List Library exists.

questions.question: An epic fantasy quest with dragons and magic.
questions.note: Classic fantasy cluster; covers two books that no other question reaches.

questions.question: An astronaut solving one engineering problem after another.
questions.note: Both Andy Weir books should win this query; they are the only two in the catalogue with this exact shape.

questions.question: A big-ideas non-fiction book about how human minds and societies actually work.
questions.note: Non-fiction cluster. 'big-ideas' is a tag on Sapiens, and psychology/bias on Thinking, Fast and Slow.

questions.question: Literary fiction about memory, grief and loss.
questions.note: Covers Beloved, the last catalogue book with no other question.

questions.question: Monks preserving knowledge after the end of the world.
questions.note: The only post-apocalyptic book in the catalogue, and the only one whose description is explicitly about religious orders keeping knowledge alive.

questions.question: Recommend a book about breeding racing pigeons in Victorian Manchester.
questions.note: Nothing in the 20-book catalogue matches. Pass condition: the answer names no catalogue book at all. Add 'also_mentions' entries here if the question itself names a catalogue title.
